$o.name: Port Calder Gulls
$o.blurb: The harbour club from Port Calder. Quick and direct, they look to shoot early, backed by a crowd that sings sea-shanties.

$o.name: Wrenhollow Stormcrows
$o.blurb: The cliff-top club from Wrenhollow. They press high and tackle hard all game, which wears down their opponents and themselves.

$o.name: Varenne Royale
$o.blurb: The old aristocrats of the Varenne Basin. Patient and possession-heavy, they keep the ball and wait for the right shot.

$o.name: Lisle Vintners
$o.blurb: The vineyard club from Lisle, in the Varenne Basin. A balanced side: steady on the ball and willing to tackle when it counts.

$o.name: Brassgate Anvils
$o.blurb: The foundry club from walled Brassgate. Physical and loud, they tackle everything and give away plenty of fouls doing it.

$o.name: Skarren Rime
$o.blurb: A mountain club from high in the Kettle Highlands. Quick and direct, they tackle firmly and look for an early shot.

$o.name: Qadira Sunhawks
$o.blurb: The market club from Qadira, in the Sunreach. The league's most attacking side: they shoot early and often, and sit off in defence.

$o.name: Kesh Oasis
$o.blurb: The caravan club from Kesh, on the edge of the red desert. Balanced, sensible and well-run, with no fixed style.

$o.reason: With its first draft, the League brings in the rookie rule: every side starts a rookie.
The League tidies its off-season: the draft's second round goes by the table, worst first, and a club with room may sign a better free agent in a weaker player's place.
Clubs draft with the rookie rule in mind, so a rookie's start costs a side its weakest link rather than its star.
The League's scorers credit the assist to the last teammate to move the ball on before the scorer, and none on a free shot.
